memory_candidates.content: To unit-test a bash helper function newly added to a larger script without polluting a real repository or performing a real network/library write: extract just the function body (grep -n for its start/end lines, then sed -n '<start>,<end>p' into a temp file), source it into a small test harness that overrides path-derived globals (e.g. GIT_ROOT, LITERATURE_DIR) to point at a temp sandbox directory, and define any ambient functions it calls (e.g. log()) as stubs. This verifies real logic (not a mock) while guaranteeing zero side effects on the actual repo -- confirmed useful when a plan's verification criteria ask for behavior (e.g. a quota-cache matrix) that would otherwise require real writes to a shared-state file like specs/zotero-index.json.

scripts/generate-context-line-counts.sh --write (and similar whole-repo drift-fix scripts) recompute/rewrite EVERY extension's index-entries.json, not just the one whose docs changed. Running it in --write mode while other tasks are concurrently dispatched in the same working tree risks introducing unrelated line_count changes into files outside your own file_scope, some of which may overlap a concurrently-dispatched sibling's declared territory. Prefer a surgical, single-entry Edit to the specific line_count field(s) that actually changed (confirmed via wc -l) over running a repo-wide --write pass during concurrent multi-task orchestration; reserve the bulk --write mode for a solo, non-concurrent maintenance pass.
